relevance_note: Single case report of a boy with Blau syndrome whose 'Genetic study confirmed an autosomal dominant mutation in the NOD2/CARD15 gene.'
method_note: Read and transcribed by hand (no table in the paper); the build script only assembles hand-entered values. Two in-scope people: the patient (single case, label 'patient') and his mother, included as an affected relative described in relation to him ('His mother had been misdiagnosed as having rheumatoid arthritis as a child, after presenting similar symptoms.'); she was not reported as tested, so she has no variant row; her 'similar symptoms' are not specified, so she has no feature rows and all checklist items are not reported; her disease label is left not reported because 'rheumatoid arthritis' is described as a misdiagnosis and the authors do not state her diagnosis. The NOD2 variant is not described (only 'an autosomal dominant mutation in the NOD2/CARD15 gene'), so variant_original_string is 'not reported'; zygosity and inheritance left not reported ('autosomal dominant' describes the mode of inheritance, not a stated zygosity, and no parental testing is reported). n_patients_reported left null because the authors state no number. Age at last evaluation recorded as the age at presentation ('13-year-old'); the last follow-up was 3 months after onset with no age given. Ocular checklist items (uveitis, cataract, glaucoma, visual impairment) excluded from the broad statement 'He had never presented ocular manifestations.'. Fever excluded from 'He denied fever ... over the previous weeks' (time-limited statement at presentation). 'no spleen or liver enlargement' excludes splenomegaly but not the composite 'hepatomegaly or hepatic granulomas' (left not reported); 'no cranial nerve involvement' does not exclude the composite 'cranial or other neuropathy' (left not reported). Arthritis checklist observed from the history of recurrent arthritis although no inflamed joints were present at the neurological presentation (recorded as a separate excluded feature, not a contradiction). 'Blood analyses were unremarkable, except for a high erythrocyte sedimentation rate' is a general normal result; no specific blood abnormality is excluded from it. Neurological features are attributed by the authors to an etanercept-induced myelopathy, not to Blau syndrome; they are recorded as observed for the patient. No contradictions found.

span: The patient had been treated earlier with corticosteroids and methotrexate and, over the previous 8 years, since the diagnosis, had also received etanercept, with good disease control.
The patient received intravenous methylprednisolone pulse therapy (1 g/day) during 5 days, followed by oral prednisone starting at 1 mg/kg, with slow dose tapering for 6 weeks.
His baseline treatment was switched to corticosteroids and methotrexate.
